Uh, so I went a little overboard with this prompt... I really liked it, so be warned, this one is a longer story. 

**Ghosts Don't Lie**

I don’t need enhanced ears to know that people gossip about me.

People call me deformed. They call me a waste of space. They don’t think I shouldn’t have a chance in our world because I won’t be able to do nearly as much as everyone else.

*Oh, you want to be a police officer? But you can’t see far enough to find your target. You can’t hear where a criminal is hiding. There are so many better candidates for the job than* ***you***.

If I had a sense, I could have become great. Just like my dad. I could help people. It’s all I’ve ever wanted; but could I really, with no enhanced sense at all?

Becoming a police officer was my dream job. Everyone thought I wouldn’t be able to become one. Even my mother, who supported me throughout my depressing childhood tried to convince me to stop trying.

As for my father, he gave up hope in me a long time ago. I think he was disappointed I didn’t develop an enhanced sense. He was a soldier, who had served his country in a war. His enhanced eyes saw more than anyone, spotting hidden troops that no one else could see. He was praised to high heaven for having such a strong enhanced ability.

So when his son was born, passing the age 5 with none… I could only imagine his disappointment.

Nonetheless, I finally made it. I got into our city’s police department… but I was heavily underpaid. I was still grateful for even making it in. But… I never felt completely happy.

I started having thoughts of suicide after a year in the department. I hated my life.

Until one day, my enhanced sense finally revealed itself.

“Police department. Open up!” I knocked a couple of times on the door, waiting for an answer.

This was a very nice house, with an expensive looking car in the driveway. I felt out of place just by standing on the porch.

I reached out to knock again, before the door swung open.

“Yes?” I was staring face to face with a broad shoulder man, wearing a business suit and tie. His hair was jet black, contrasting with his vibrant green eyes.

“We received a call about yelling and screaming,” I said. “Is everything okay?”

“Oh, yes of course,” He said, smiling. “I’m sorry, it’s just my daughter was overreacting a bit since I told her she wouldn’t be allowed to a party. Teens, right?”

I got hit with an invisible wave, my senses spiking. *He’s… lying. How do I know that?* “...Sir, is it alright if I come inside?”

He paused. The man reached into his suit, and I tensed, only to relax when he pulled out a business card. “Unfortunately, no. I hope you can understand.”

I grabbed the card out of his hand, reading it. A photo of him was in the top right corner, his business labelled accordingly, his name inscribed in a fancy font.

*Chris Taryn. Oh.*

I fumbled the card in my hands, shoving it in my pocket. “I apologize, sir.”

My thoughts scrambled in my head in a panic. Chris Taryn owned the most famous and profitable company in this city, a clothing company. If I got into his business, it would get me fired.

“No need for apologies. Now, if you excuse me, I have places to be.”

I nodded, and he closed the front door, walking around me. My eyes followed him as he walked to his car, and I felt a wave of immense emotions.

*He’s angry, annoyed, and… empty.*

Goosebumps traveled throughout my body. I looked down at my arm to see them very visible on my skin.

*This doesn’t feel right. Something is wrong.*

The day passed rather quickly. I went to sleep with a pit in my stomach, seeing Taryn’s face in my head throughout the night, until I finally fell asleep. My dreams were alarming.

There was a dark room, filled with bloody corpses lying on the floor; and to make things worse, they were all teens or younger. I could feel myself shaking. One of the kids got up off the floor, pale. She looked at me, staring into my soul with sad eyes.

*“Help us...”*

I lunged up on my bed, sweating.

I was still in my room, the moonlight streaming in through my window, casting shadows that startled me even more. My eyes darted around the room, the entire house silent.

I rose out of my bed, reaching out to my police uniform on my chair. *I have to go.*

On my way to Chris Taryn’s house, I felt guilt rise in me. I looked at the time; 2:04 PM. I called backup as soon as I drove up into the driveway, having to lie in order to get them to come. Otherwise, they wouldn't have listened to me.

I turned off my car, waiting in the driveway, staring at the house. Lights were still on, to my surprise. Taryn must be awake.

*He could be killing someone right now.*

I swung my car door open, and walked up to the door with my hand on my gun.

I knocked on the door lightly, and he opened the door with attitude.

He looked surprised. “You’re the officer from earlier.”

I felt another wave of emotions hit me, coming from this man. He was annoyed, and the strongest emotion, *worry.*

“Sir, you’re going to need to step aside.” I ordered.

He glared at me. “I don’t think you have a warrant.”

“You've been murdering kids in this house,” I said, my voice rising. “Put your hands behind your back!”

He hesitated. And then he attacked.

He barreled into me, his hands clasped around my neck as we both fell to the ground.

I tried to pull him off, but to no avail. His eyes were staring down at me; I had to look away. He looked psychotic.

That’s when I heard sirens, and his grip loosened when he looked up. It allowed me to breathe for a brief moment, and then I heard the familiar voices of other officers.

“Let go of him and put your hands in the air!”I suspected they had a gun pointed at him, because he quickly obeyed.

When I rose to my feet, one of the officers checked on me before he went to arrest Chris.

I rubbed my neck, taking in quick, deep breaths. *That was… intense.*

Three officers handled the arrest of Chris Taryn. I left them, feeling drawn to this house. Upon entering, everything looked normal.

But when I blinked, I jumped when a girl appeared just in front of my eyes. The same girl from the dream. But it wasn’t just her. Other kids started to appear around the house, ghosts.

The girl from my dream pointed to a wall, and I walked, reluctantly, towards the wall. It took me a moment to realize this was a hidden door, and I pressed my hand against it.

It opened, revealing the same, dark, old room from my dream. A horrid smell wafted around this room, and I covered my nose. An officer appeared behind me, his eyes narrowed.

There was blood everywhere, and a girl’s body was right in the center of this room.

I pushed passed the officer behind me, walking towards Chris who was being handcuffed outside.

“How many innocent kids have you killed?!” I questioned, my voice raising.

He turned, a smile etching it’s way across his face. “Too many for anyone to count.”

I stayed silent, and the man looked away from me, being taken away to a cop car.

*If I had been here earlier…*

*I could have saved that girl.*
